info.name: Storefront API
info.description:
Every route of the storefront API, generated from `openapi.yaml`.

**Sessions:** Register, Login and Refresh store `accessToken` in a collection variable, and the
refresh token arrives as an HttpOnly cookie that Postman keeps in its cookie jar — so Refresh and
Logout work without pasting anything.

**Admin:** run *Auth → Log in as admin* once (after `npm run seed:admin`); every request under
Admin uses the `adminAccessToken` it stores.

Ids captured from responses (`productId`, `orderId`, `cartItemId`, …) feed the requests that need them.

request.description:
Health check

Answers while the server is up. The only route outside the envelope.

Register an account

Creates a `customer` account and signs it in. A `role` sent in the body is ignored —
self-registration can never create an admin.

`firstName` falls back to the username and `lastName` to an empty string when omitted.
Usernames are compared case-insensitively, so `Alice` and `alice` are the same account.

Returns the access token in the body and sets the refresh cookie.

Log in

Exchanges credentials for an access token, and sets the refresh cookie.

A wrong username and a wrong password answer the same way, and take the same time,
so neither reveals which accounts exist. The attempt is recorded in the audit log
with the username that was tried — never the password.
Signs in the account created by `npm run seed:admin` and stores its token as `adminAccessToken`, which every request under Admin uses.

Renew the session

Reads the refresh cookie, issues a new access token and rotates the cookie. Send it
with credentials; there is no request body.

Rotation is single-use: the token in the cookie is invalidated as it is exchanged.
Presenting an already-exchanged token means it was copied, so the whole session is
revoked and `auth.refresh_token_reuse` is recorded in the audit log.

Log out of this session

Revokes the session the refresh cookie belongs to and clears the cookie. Answers
`200` even without a cookie, so a client can always finish signing out.

Log out everywhere

Deletes every refresh token of the signed-in account and clears the cookie.
The signed-in account

Your account

The account the token belongs to, with its five most recent purchases. Any other id
answers `403`, for an admin token too — `/admin/users/{id}` is the way to read
another account.

Update your profile

Changes `firstName`, `lastName` or `username` — at least one of them. The role and
the password are not accepted here: the password has its own route below, so a
profile update can never change credentials or privileges.

Close your account

Scrubs the profile, deletes the addresses and cart, and ends every session. The row
itself stays so the orders placed with it keep an owner, and the username is freed
for someone else. The account can no longer sign in, and reads answer `404`.

Change your password

Takes the current password as well as the new one, so a stolen access token alone
cannot lock the owner out. Every other session of the account ends, and the reply
carries a fresh access token and refresh cookie so this client stays signed in.

request.description:
Browse the catalog

Products that are on sale, newest ids last. Filtering happens on the server, so a
page only ever holds matching products. Archived products are not listed here.

Most bought products

The five products with the highest quantity across **completed** orders, so an order
that was never checked out cannot promote a product. Archived products are left out.

Every category on sale

The distinct categories of products that are on sale, sorted A–Z.

One product

A product that is on sale. An archived product answers `404` here.

query.description: Page size. Bounded so one request cannot pull a whole table.

request.description:
Your orders

Orders belonging to the token user, newest first, each with the total it was charged.
There is no route here that creates or changes an order: checkout creates them, and
`/admin/orders` is where they are managed.

One of your orders

Someone else's order answers `404`, so its existence is never revealed.

What an order holds

The lines of one of your orders. Each line keeps the price charged at the time
(`unitPrice`) and the option that was chosen (`typeId`), so a later price change
does not alter the order.

Your cart

Every row in the token user's cart, each with the product it points at.

Put something in the cart

Adds a product, or an option of it named by `typeId`. The same product and option
twice adds up the quantities (capped at 999).

The option, its price and the shop are read from the product; a price or option sent
in the body is ignored. A product that does not exist or is archived answers `400`.
Empty the cart

Change a quantity

A row that is not yours answers `404`.

item.name: Take a row out of the cart

request.description: Take a row out of the cart

Your addresses

The default address first, then the rest oldest first.

Save an address

The first address saved becomes the default one. Saving another with
`isDefault: true` moves the default over to it.
One of your addresses

Change an address

At least one field. An address that is not yours answers `404` and changes nothing —
including your own default, which the update checks ownership before touching.

Delete an address

Deleting the default one hands the default to the oldest address that is left.

request.description:
Report a page the user opened

The frontend calls this on each navigation. The row lands in `page_views`, which
admins read with `GET /admin/page-views`; it leaves no entry in the audit log.

query.description: Page size. Bounded so one request cannot pull a whole table.

request.description:
List accounts

Every open account. Closed accounts are not listed.

Create an account

Unlike self-registration, this may set the role.

One account

The account with its five most recent purchases. Recorded in the audit log.

Update a profile

Profile fields only. The role and the password have their own routes.

Close an account

Scrubs the profile, deletes the addresses and cart and ends every session, keeping
the row so its orders keep an owner. An admin cannot close their own account here.

Change a role

Ends every session of that account, so the old privilege cannot be renewed. An admin
cannot change their own role, which keeps the last admin from locking themselves out.

Reset a password

Sets a new password without the old one, and ends every session of that account.
The admin's own session is untouched.

query.description: Page size. Bounded so one request cannot pull a whole table.

request.description:
List every product

Archived products included, which `/products` leaves out.

Add a product

Every field is checked, including the entries of `types` and `reviews`, so a
malformed value cannot reach the database and break later reads of the catalog.

Add many products

Takes an array of 1–500 products and saves them in one transaction: if one of them
is wrong, none of them are saved.
One product, archived or not

Change a product

Changes only the fields it is given — at least one of them. Setting
`isActive: true` puts an archived product back on sale.

Archive a product

Takes the product off sale (`isActive: false`) instead of deleting the row, so the
order lines that point at it keep working. `PATCH` with `isActive: true` undoes it.
